organization.name: Mount Sinai Health System
organization.short_description: Mount Sinai Health System is one of the largest academic medical systems in New York City, encompassing eight hospitals, a leading medical school, and a vast network of ambulatory practices. Known for pioneering research and clinical innovation.

contactAnalysis.name: Kristin Myers
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Information Officer & SVP
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CIO with system-wide authority over technology investments — key budget holder for AI infrastructure.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Engage after building credibility with Eric Schadt's team. Present infrastructure and scaling strategy for clinical AI deployment.

contactAnalysis.name: Eric Schadt
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Data Scientist & Dean, AI and Human Health
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Chief Data Scientist and Dean of AI — direct authority over AI strategy and investment. The most important stakeholder in any AI deal.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Connect through academic channels, conference presentations, or research collaboration opportunities. Lead with technical depth.

contactAnalysis.name: Thomas Chen
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Digital Health & Innovation
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Leads digital health innovation — would champion AI tools that accelerate Mount Sinai's innovation agenda.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: First touch target. Frame around bridging research-to-production gap — the specific challenge academic medical centers face.

contactAnalysis.name: Benjamin Glicksberg
contactAnalysis.title: Director, AI & Data Science Research
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Directs AI research and would technically evaluate any AI platform for research and clinical applications.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Technical deep-dive on capabilities that accelerate existing research. Offer joint publication opportunity.

contactAnalysis.name: Roberta Freeman
contactAnalysis.title: Chief Medical Informatics Officer
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CMIO bridges clinical practice and technology — the power buyer for clinical AI at academic medical centers. Controls what tools physicians actually adopt.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Engage alongside Eric Schadt's team. Focus on physician workflow integration — she determines if AI tools survive clinical committee review.

contactAnalysis.name: Rachel Sternberg
contactAnalysis.title: Director, Clinical Informatics
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Clinical informatics director bridges technology and clinical workflows — key evaluator for clinical AI deployment.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Partner on clinical workflow integration design. She will determine if AI fits physician and nursing workflows.

contactAnalysis.name: Mark Hoffman
contactAnalysis.title: CISO
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: CISO will enforce strict security and HIPAA requirements. Academic medical centers have heightened security scrutiny.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Proactively share security posture documentation. Address research data governance and IRB compliance concerns.

contactAnalysis.name: Patricia Walsh
contactAnalysis.title: VP, Research Compliance & Privacy
contactAnalysis.whyTheyMatter: Academic medical center compliance requires IRB review for any AI touching patient data — adds 2-3 months to deal timeline that must be planned for.
contactAnalysis.approachAngle: Proactively provide IRB-ready documentation and data governance framework. Address research data vs. clinical data handling distinctions.

signals.aiStrategy: Mount Sinai established the Hasso Plattner Institute for Digital Health — one of the most advanced clinical AI programs in the US — and has published 200+ peer-reviewed AI/ML papers across radiology, pathology, and genomics. They are actively building foundation models for clinical data across their 8-hospital system and collaborating with tech companies on federated learning and privacy-preserving AI.

plan.executiveSummary: Mount Sinai is a premier academic medical center that has invested more heavily in clinical AI than almost any other US health system — 200+ AI publications, $100M+ AI infrastructure investment, and a dedicated Dean of AI and Human Health. The play is not greenfield adoption but providing infrastructure or capabilities that accelerate their existing research-to-production pipeline across 8 hospitals and 48,000 employees. Landing Mount Sinai creates a flagship reference account that opens every academic medical center in the country.
plan.painToProductFit:
1. RESEARCH-TO-PRODUCTION GAP: Hundreds of AI models in research but deploying into clinical workflows at scale across 8 hospitals is the bottleneck.
2. CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION: 48K employees and 8 hospitals — ambient documentation and clinical NLP at scale represents massive physician time savings.
3. MULTI-SITE DATA HARMONIZATION: 8 hospitals with varying data quality and formats require AI-powered normalization.
4. OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY: Revenue cycle optimization, staffing prediction, and throughput forecasting across a $9.7B operation.
plan.competitiveThreats: PALANTIR: Already embedded with Foundry for data integration — strong incumbent. GOOGLE HEALTH: Active research collaborations with academic medical centers. MICROSOFT/NUANCE: DAX Copilot likely already deployed or in pilot for documentation. INTERNAL TEAMS: World-class AI research team may prefer building on their own infrastructure. EPIC: Expanding AI within EHR reduces demand for external solutions.
plan.timingUrgency: Recent $100M+ AI infrastructure investment means budget is allocated and being deployed NOW. Expanding clinical AI from research pilots to system-wide deployment requires new tooling. Other academic medical centers (Mayo, Cleveland Clinic, Mass General Brigham) are racing to deploy — Mount Sinai must maintain leadership.
plan.dealStrategy: Research-first entry over 4-8 months. Phase 1: Connect with Eric Schadt's team through academic channels or conference presentations. Phase 2: Technical deep-dive with Benjamin Glicksberg on research acceleration. Phase 3: Bridge to clinical deployment through Thomas Chen (Digital Health). Phase 4: Executive alignment with CIO Kristin Myers on infrastructure strategy. Phase 5: Joint pilot with publication opportunity. Estimated deal size: $500K-2M initial, $5M+ enterprise. Risks: sophisticated buyers, long evaluation, publication requirements.
plan.discoveryQuestions:
1. What's your biggest bottleneck in moving AI models from research into clinical production?
2. How do you currently handle data harmonization across your 8 hospital sites?
3. What infrastructure are you using for ML training and inference at scale?
4. How important is the ability to publish results when evaluating new AI partnerships?
5. What are your top 3 priorities for clinical AI deployment this year?
plan.roiFramework: Clinical documentation AI: Save 2 hours/physician/day across 5,000+ physicians = $300M+ annually. Predictive analytics: 15% reduction in readmissions = ~$50M in avoided penalties. ED triage optimization: 20% improvement in throughput = significant revenue impact. Research acceleration: Reduce model development cycle from 6 months to 6 weeks. PILOT: 90-day pilot with one clinical department (radiology or pathology), joint paper on results.
